utpfs7:262: The most intractable problem in the collision model is information asymmetry: independent researchers have no telemetry, no customer logs, no threat intelligence feeds, and cannot determine whether the bug they report is already being exploited in the wild. The pragmatic strategy the author offers is "assume the worst"—by default you are not the sole discoverer; submit the report as soon as possible and apply pressure to shorten the disclosure window; if the vendor stalls, throw the responsibility back to the vendor. Meanwhile, Linus's criticism of drive-by reports reveals another survival strategy: read the documentation, write a patch, add real value on top of AI output. Reports with patches not only get fixed faster, but also accumulate "trust capital"—the next time that letter enters the vendor's inbox, it receives priority treatment. This essentially shifts a researcher's competitiveness from "discovery speed" to "delivery quality."
